articles.headline: Bishop Payne's Appeal in behalf of the Wilberforce University
articles.author: Daniel A. Payne
articles.summary: To the ministry, the laity, and the friends of the A. M. E. Church throughout the United States of America. Dear Brethren: This is to inform you, that the beautiful property of the Wilberforce University, is now offered to us for the sum of [amount blurred]. This property was bought in the summer of 1856, and a school opened for the special benefit of the colored people.

articles.summary: To the Philadelphia and New England Conferences. To the members and friends. The Philadelphia Annual Conference will meet the second Saturday in May, at 9 o'clock A. M., in Bethel Church, Sixth St., Phila. The New England Conference will meet the second Saturday in June, in Newport, R. I.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Wesley M. E. Church, Lombard St.)
articles.author: John A. Williams
articles.summary: Phila., Friday, April 3d, 1863. Rev. John A. Williams, pastor of the first Wesley M. E. Church, in Lombard St. between Fifth and Sixth, Phila., will hold his last Quarterly Meeting in this Conference year, ending on the 2d of May, at 4 o'clock, P. M.

articles.headline: Sabbath School Convention (committee called)
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: The Committee who was appointed to draw up a Constitution and By-Laws, are called upon to meet in Bethel church, Philadelphia, on the 8th inst., by order of Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Chairman.

articles.headline: Bethel Sabbath School Presentation
articles.summary: The thoughtful Christian gentleman, L. R. Seymour, the superintendent of the Bethel Sabbath school, presented on last Wednesday, on behalf of the Sabbath school committee and teachers, $20.00 for the Christian Recorder.

articles.headline: City Items: Rev. Mr. Gibbs recovering
articles.summary: The Rev. Mr. Gibbs is getting better, and in a few days will be able to resume his labors. We labored for him on last Sabbath afternoon. His members still seem to keep up interest.

articles.headline: Confirmation (St. Thomas' Church)
articles.summary: In the evening we attended the services at St. Thomas' Church, of which Rev. Wm. Alston is Rector. We met, while on the way to the church, quite a number, who said that they could not gain admittance.
people: seated the editor ('a lady of much distinction')

articles.headline: Colored Men Soldiers for the War, and the 54th Mass. Regiment
articles.summary: Those men who are engaged in helping to raise men for the 54th, are quite active; two, three and four times a week there are taken from Mr. Jordan's, from twenty to thirty at a time, to go and join the 54th Massachusetts regiment.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscriptions)
articles.summary: Cold Spring Harbor, L. I., Chas. Bristol, 2.25. Frankfort, Pa. William S. Walker, 1.00. Chatham, C. W. Rev. Wm. H. Jones, 2.50. Medford, N. J. Mr. James T. Still, 2.25.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (worn-out preachers' collection)
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Feb. 2d, 1863, received of Rev. Theodore Gould, pastor of the Princeton charge, for the worn-out preachers' collection, the sum of $2.00. March 21st, received of Rev. William R. Norris, of Reading circuit, for said worn-out preachers' collection.

articles.headline: Died (Rev. Spencer Logan)
articles.summary: On Thursday last, at one o'clock, Rev. Spencer Logan, of the Philadelphia Conference, departed this life; a more extended notice will be given in our next issue.

articles.headline: City Items: Mass Meeting of Colored People (54th Massachusetts)
articles.summary: As our city papers have a pretty full report of our meeting, we clip the following, which answers to our note: A mass meeting of colored people, to take action to fill the 54th Massachusetts Colored Regiment, was held last evening, at Franklin Hall. (Also named, reading uncertain: William E. Gibson [VERIFY] (vice president (Esq.)); David B. Bowser [VERIFY] (vice president); David Bustill [VERIFY] (speaker ('colored')).)

articles.headline: An Address delivered at the Exhibition in the A. M. E. Union Church (Subject: Youth)
articles.author: Wm. Tune Simpson [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Delivered at the exhibition in the A. M. E. Union Church, on the evening of April 2d, 1863. Subject: 'Youth.' In the midst of health and youth, the pleasures and enticements of the world are apt to appear a very gay and pleasing scene. Dated A. M. E. Union Church, Sabbath School, Phila. Pa., Apr. 4th, 1863.

articles.headline: Notice: Bishop Nazrey to preach at the Mission Church, West Phila.
articles.summary: Bishop Nazrey will preach at the Mission Church, West Phila., to-morrow, (Sabbath) for Rev. W. D. W. Schureman.
people: pastor, Mission Church, West Philadelphia (Rev.; printed 'Schureman')

articles.headline: Notice: Camden Circuit fourth quarterly meeting
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: Camden Circuit, fourth quarterly meeting, commences on Friday evening, 24th inst., and will continue every evening until the following Monday. Quarterly Conference will be held at Macedonia Church, on Saturday afternoon, the 25th inst., at 3 o'clock. Quarterly meeting at Woodbury, on Saturday and Sunday, the 2d and 3d of May. April 10th, 1863.

articles.headline: Died (Rev. Spencer Logan)
articles.summary: The Rev. Spencer Logan, of the Philadelphia conference, departed this life on Thursday evening, the 2d inst. Brother Logan had not been in the itinerant work a great while. Nearly two years ago, he ruptured a blood-vessel, which prostrated him for some time.
people: deceased (Rev.), superannuated member of the Philadelphia Conference
spoke at the funeral, Bethel Church (Rev.)
spoke at the funeral, Bethel Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Philadelphia Items (Zion Wesley quarterly meeting)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath was the last quarterly meeting of Rev. Mr. Williams, of Zion Wesley Church. The Rev. Mr. Reeves preached at 10 1/2 o'clock, A. M., from the words, 'Why seek ye the living among the dead; he is risen,' &c. He gave us a very interesting discourse.

articles.headline: Died (Rev. Charles C. Gardiner of Harrisburg)
articles.summary: The Rev. Charles C. Gardiner of Harrisburg, Pa., who was pastor of the Presbyterian Church, (Colored,) departed this life on the 6th inst., at his late residence in Harrisburg, in the 84th year of his age. His disease was dropsy. He was brought on to Philadelphia, and placed in the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church.
people: deceased (Rev.), pastor of the Presbyterian Church (colored), Harrisburg, Pa.

articles.headline: Annual Conference (Ohio, Baltimore, Philadelphia dates)
articles.summary: The Ohio Annual Conference will meet on the 18th of this month, in Springfield, Ohio. Bishop Quinn will preside. Bishops Payne and Nazrey are expected to be present. The Baltimore Conference will meet on the 23d of April. The Philadelphia Conference will meet on the second Saturday in May. Bishop Nazrey will preside.

articles.headline: Boarding House (Mr. and Mrs. Cropper)
articles.summary: Mr. and Mrs. Cropper have opened up a Boarding House for the accommodation of our people, in Lombard Street, No. 403, between Fourth and Fifth Streets. They have done this because so many of our people travelling through the city are put to such great inconvenience in getting accommodations.
people: boarding-house keepers, Lombard St. between Fourth and Fifth (ad names 'Mr. & Mrs. H. M. Cropper') (printed 'Mr. and Mrs. Cropper')

articles.headline: Alumni Association: Frederick Douglass lecture (editorial notice)
articles.summary: The Alumni Association have consummated an arrangement to have Mr. Frederick Douglass lecture for them on the 24th inst., at the National Hall. This is a worthy cause, and every colored lady and gentleman should lay by twenty-five cents, get a ticket, and go to the lecture.

articles.headline: National Hall: Frederick Douglass will lecture before the Alumni Association of the Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: National Hall. Frederick Douglass will lecture before the Alumni Association of the Institute for Colored Youth, on Friday evening, April 24th, at National Hall. Subject, 'The Affairs of the Nation.' Tickets of Admission, 25 cents. Tickets can be had at the office of the Lebanon Cemetery, 717 Lombard Street. Also at Mr. Weaver's Book Store, 619 Pine Street.
people: ticket agent, Book Store, 619 Pine Street (printed 'Mr. Weaver's')

articles.headline: Married (Studum and Benson)
articles.summary: On the 9th of March, 1863, by Rev. Elisha Weaver, Mr. William J. Studum [VERIFY], of Lancaster, to Miss Elizabeth B. Benson, of Phila.

articles.headline: A Gracious and Timely Presentation
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: We have the extreme honor and gratification to acknowledge the thoughtful and Christian presentation of a fine and splendid suit of cloth and satin clothes, by the following inestimable ladies: Miss Mary Still, Mrs. Ann Lawe, Mrs. Eliza Stokely, Miss Jane Moulter [VERIFY] of Germantown, and Miss Esther Armstrong of Philadelphia, on the 1?th day of April, 1863.
people: encouraged the gift (printed 'Rev. Mrs. Stephen Smith')

articles.headline: Union, Its Desirableness
articles.summary: We went to say in behalf of the Presbyterian and Baptist churches; We have had the extreme pleasure of preaching for those churches. This is what we love. ... If we were to stay in Philadelphia ten years, we would have no other desire than to keep up just such a union as there is between Revs. Gibbs, Reeves, and Hamilton of the Baptist Church, and others.

articles.headline: Items: Camden communion; Gardiner notice; Bethel's Sabbath
articles.summary: Last Sabbath we were in Camden to administer the Lord's supper for Rev. Peter Gardiner, who has been indisposed for several weeks. ... We will give a more extended account of the death of Rev. Charles Gardiner in our next. Bethel A. M. E. Church, on last Sabbath, enjoyed a treat.

articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: The close of the pastor's biennial labor in the A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, Phila., will be, viz., on Sunday, the 26th inst., at 10 1/2 o'clock, A. M. Love feast; doors open at half-past 9 o'clock. Preaching at 3 o'clock, P. M., subject, 'The three whats connected with the believer's redemption.' At 7 1/2 o'clock, P. M., a valedictory address will be delivered.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscriptions; New Jersey circuits)

articles.author: James L. Thomas
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: The Union Relief Association begs leave to acknowledge through the Recorder, the receipt of the following goods, &c., for the relief of the freedmen, in and around Washington. One box and a barrel of goods from Union Church, Philadelphia, Rev. Henry Davis, pastor. ... From Bethel Church of Philadelphia, Rev. J. P. Campbell, pastor, twelve dollars and sixty cents in cash.

articles.author: W. H. S.
articles.summary: The Southern Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Zion connexion, convened in Zion Wesley Church, Washington City, D. C., on Saturday, April 11th, at 4 o'clock, P. M., Rt. Rev. Joseph J. Clinton, Superintendent, "Second District," presiding. The delegation from the several Conferences was, on motion, granted all the privileges of the Conference. J. P. articles.headline: Our Colored Soldiers (sentiments of the Annual Conference, Philadelphia district)
articles.summary: Sentiments of the Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church, (Philadelphia district) in relation to colored soldiers; preamble: Whereas, We have witnessed with the deepest interest, the self-sacrificing and heroic devotion of those men of color, our brethren, acquaintances, and friends, who have left home and friends in answer to the call of the President of these United States, through Governor Andrew of Massachusetts...

articles.headline: Lecture (William Anderson of Jamaica at Bethel Church)
articles.summary: We call attention to the lecture of William Anderson, Esq., of the Island of Jamaica, to be held in Bethel Church, 6th Street, Philadelphia, on next Monday evening. It is to be hoped that the house will be filled, for we expect Mr. Anderson who has been for the last thirty years in the West Indies, and can give us rich information, relative to that country.

articles.headline: Notice: Bethel Sabbath School grand concert for Wilberforce University
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:-The teachers of Bethel Sabbath School, together with a number of scholars of the same, intend giving a grand concert of vocal music, at Sansom Street Hall, on Thursday evening, 28th inst., in aid of the purchase of the Wilberforce University. The singing will be under the conductorship of Prof. H. Shadd. Mr. Seymoor will preside at the piano. (Also named, reading uncertain: Daniel T. Masten [VERIFY] (committee chairman); Abram Fields [VERIFY] (committee).)

articles.headline: The Bethel Exhibition (date change)
articles.summary: The Bethel Exhibition is on Wednesday, the 27th inst., instead of Thursday, the 28th.

articles.headline: An Essay, read by one of the Sabbath School teachers of Bethel A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia
articles.author: Drusilla Rodgers [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Divine influence has very little advancement at present, among the younger portion of this assembly. What is the reason, is a question often asked. Is there none to answer?

articles.headline: To Carrie (poem on the Institute for Colored Youth examination)
articles.author: R. B. Jones
articles.summary: The Institute for colored youth / In Philadelphia / Much talent did display, forsooth, / About the first of May. Five members of the senior class, / Examination stood. (Dated Ashmun Institute, May 18th, 1863.) (Also named, reading uncertain: Carrie E. Le Count [VERIFY] (ICY senior-class student who 'did all the rest excel').)

articles.headline: Notice of Quarterly Meetings (West Chester circuit)
articles.author: Jeremiah Young
articles.summary: At West Chester, June 13th and 14th. At Westtown, June 20th and 21st. At Thornbury, June 27th and 28th. At Media, July 4th and 5th. At Unionville(?), July 11th and 12th. At Lamberton(?), July 18th and 19th. Jeremiah Young, Elder in Charge. West Chester, May 25th, 1863.

articles.headline: Notice: Dr. H. Jerome Brown's lecture at Union Baptist Church
articles.author: James Hamilton
articles.summary: By request Dr. H. Jerome Brown will deliver another of his interesting Scientific Lectures on Moral and Intellectual Physiology, in the Union Baptist Church, Little Pine street, Tuesday evening next, June 2d. The lecture will be finely illustrated with a collection of life-size paintings. Admission free, commencing at 8 o'clock.

articles.headline: Notice: Pastoral appointments in the Union A.M.E. Church
articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: Pastoral appointments in the Union A. M. E. Church. On Sunday, 31st inst., 10 1/2 o'clock, A. M. The first lecture of a course on affliction, will be delivered: Theme, 'The chastening rod in the Father's hand.' At 8 o'clock, P. M. a sermon will be delivered: Theme, 'Angelic Agency.'

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers (editorial)
articles.summary: We understand that the colored soldiers of the 54th Massachusetts Regiment have gone South, and that no better drilled regiment has left the North... We did hope that they would come through Philadelphia, that we might have an opportunity of beholding a sight never before witnessed in this country.
people: bishop; visited the colored regiment's encampment on Mason's Island (printed 'Bishop Payne')

articles.headline: Wilberforce University (Philadelphia District effort)
articles.summary: The Philadelphia District will make a very strong effort to raise their proportion. In a cause of so great a moment to our people we would like to know who it is that is not willing to make great efforts to secure that property, for we are determined to have it with the help of God.

articles.headline: Lecture (W. W. Anderson at Wesley Church, report)
articles.summary: The lecture announced last week was delivered by the Hon. W. W. Anderson on Monday night at Wesley Church. We had the pleasure of introducing his Honor to the audience. He commenced by referring to the war in this country, and contrasted our condition previous to the war with that of England.

articles.headline: Grand Concert (Bethel Sabbath School, for Wilberforce University, report)
articles.summary: A grand concert came off on last Wednesday night in Sansom Street Hall, for the benefit of the Wilberforce University, a most praiseworthy object. The audience was not so large as we would have liked to see it.

articles.headline: The Recorder and the procuring of subscribers
articles.summary: We should like to see all of our ministers take as deep an interest in the Christian Recorder as Sister Frances Valentine, who, while on a visit to Allentown, procured some three cash subscribers. Good for her.

articles.headline: Mass Meeting of the Order of Good Samaritans (resolutions on Edward M. Thomas)
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:-A Mass Meeting of the members of District Grand Lodge No. 2, of the Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, was held at the new Masonic Hall, South 11th st., Philadelphia, on Monday evening, April 20th, 1863. Wm. H. Longfellow was chosen chairman, and Jonathan Davis, secretary.
people: secretary; also printed 'Dr. Jonathan Davis', who addressed the meeting

J. J. Clinton.

articles.headline: An Incident (Green and Coates St. passenger car)
articles.summary: A few evenings since, an incident occurred on one of the Green and Coates St. passenger cars, which is worthy of record: A colored woman with a child in one arm and a basket in the other, hailed a car and asked the conductor if she could ride. The conductor immediately stopped the car, and addressed the passengers as follows:-'Ladies and gentlemen, here is a colored woman with a basket and child who wants to ride; have you any objections?' One unanimous no, rang through the car.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (Mount Laurel, N.J. and Frankford, Pa. entries)
articles.summary: Acknowledgments of money received for the Recorder and books, by place (Xenia, Ohio Conference ministers, Pittsburgh, Allegheny City, Boston and others), including Mount Laurel, N. J., and Frankford, Pa.

articles.headline: Notice (Peter D. Bundick warns against trusting his wife)
articles.author: Peter D. Bundick
articles.summary: The public are hereby warned not to trust my wife, Ann Maria T. Bundick, as I will not pay any debts of her contracting, she having left my bed and board without any just cause. Peter D. Bundick. April 30th, 1863.

articles.headline: Sabbaths in Philadelphia (Lombard Street groggeries; Sunday tavern closing)
articles.summary: Twenty-five years ago, when Lombard St., from Fifth to Eighth was blessed with a respectable class of colored persons and property holders, the neighborhood was blessed with quiet Sabbaths; and as the colored churches were ranged in and about one square from this location, with decent pavements and quiet sidewalks, we could enjoy a very pleasant walk with friends to and from our churches, and sit at our front doors without our ears being saluted with profane language.

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Annual Conference met this morning (editorial note)
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference met this morning, at 9 o'clock, A. M., in Bethel church, Sixth St.; Bishop Nazrey will preside, and will be assisted by Bishops Quinn and Payne. It is hoped that we shall have a good time.

articles.headline: Jordantown supper for the preacher
articles.author: Joseph H. Long
articles.summary: Jordantown, May 1st, 1863. Mr. Editor.-I wish to occupy a small space in your paper to inform the public that Jordantown still lives. We have this year some $50.00 on the church, and on April 30th they had a supper for the benefit of their preacher, from which they realized the sum of $28.43, which was paid over to their pastor on the same night. (Also named, reading uncertain: Louise Polk [VERIFY] (supper committee); Lucy Amos [VERIFY] (supper committee).)

articles.headline: In Memoriam (Joseph Adams of Haddonfield, N.J.)
articles.author: G. B. Miller
articles.summary: Died, April 17th, 1863, of consumption, in the 2?th year of his age, Joseph Adams, son of Luke and Phoebe Adams, of Haddonfield, New Jersey. The deceased was a young man much respected for his honest, peaceable and industrious deportment.

articles.summary: New Haven, April 26th(?), 1863. Whereas, Our beloved Pastor, Rev. William T. Catto, has asked to be relieved from his pastoral charge over us, and we reviewing his life and general deportment since he has been among us, are convinced that as a citizen, Christian, and minister, his loss to this community will be to his numerous friends a loss which we shall ever regret.

A. Payne. Conference was opened in the usual way. It was then resolved that Rev. W. D. W. Schureman be elected Secretary, and Rev. A. L. Stanford, Assistant.

articles.headline: Lecture by Rev. Mr. Logan at Wesley church (streetcar ejection)
articles.summary: We were not present at the commencement but assure our readers that what we heard, was every way interesting. He told us about the history of his life, when South, living with the men who claimed him as goods and chattel... He told a story of his arrival in our city: he stepped into our street cars, and took his seat, as he would in New York, Brooklyn, Boston or Pittsburgh, but the conductor came to him and asked him to get out and stand on the platform of the car.

articles.headline: The High School Examination (Institute for Colored Youth alumni exercises)
articles.summary: The examination of the pupils of the Institute for colored youth, came off last week. We are sorry that we could not be there on the occasion, as we had just returned home from visiting the Ohio and Baltimore Annual Conferences. But we are told that the scholars acquitted themselves handsomely, as they usually do. We had the pleasure of being at the exercises on Friday. (Also named, reading uncertain: Joseph M. White [VERIFY] (chairman, of the Alumni).)
people: read an address (printed 'Mr. J. C. White, Jr.')

articles.headline: Puff: James W. Brown's steam-dyeing business enlarged
articles.summary: We call strict attention to the business of our very gentlemanly James W. Brown, Steam-dyeing, scouring, and repairing clothing, who has enlarged his place of business, and is now carrying on his business quite extensively... His place of business is at No. 126 South Sixth St., above Walnut, and at No. 1008 Shippen St.

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Conference Minutes (editorial objections)
articles.summary: Our objections to them are three in particular. We don't like to find fault unless necessity drives us to it, which it does in these cases. First, We, for the first time in life, brought three as strong complaints against a member of the Philadelphia Conference, as language and words could make them, which would have been entertained in any civil court ... But they were ruled out by the presiding officer ... We appealed from said ruling ... to the General Conference ... Our second objection is, That we made a report of the state of the Book Concern and paper ... It also does not appear in the minutes. ... Our third objection is, That we are charged and left standing in debt for 275 minutes of last year's Annual Conference ... We would say more, but as Elders Schureman and Stanford say that they compiled the minutes, and put them in the hands of their chairman to superintend the printing ... they do not feel, and are not responsible for what was left out.

articles.headline: Newport Correspondence (Wilberforce first payment)
articles.author: Payne
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: This is to inform the church and the public that we have met our first obligation on account of the Wilberforce University. That is to say, the sum of $3000 was paid over to the proper authorities on the 11th inst., and a quit claim deed made out in behalf of the A. M. E. Church ... We also regret to state that the Philadelphia contribution of one hundred and forty-two dollars came too late to be of any use in paying the first installment.
people: Bishop; signs 'Payne' in behalf of the Institution

events.name: Wesley M. E. Church (Lombard St.) quarterly meeting and love feast
events.location: first Wesley M. E. Church, Lombard St. between Fifth and Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice dated Phila., Friday, April 3d, 1863, signed John A. Williams, Pastor: his last Quarterly Meeting of the Conference year (printed 'ending on the 2d of May, at 4 o'clock, P. M.'). Preaching Sabbath morning at 10 1/2 o'clock by Rev. Mr. Reeve, pastor of the 2d Presbyterian Church in Lombard Street; at 3 o'clock by Rev. Jacob B. Trusty; sacramental discourse at 7 o'clock by Rev. Elisha Weaver. Love Feast Wednesday evening, 'the 6th inst.' (as printed; April 6, 1863 was a Monday), doors open at 7 o'clock.

events.name: Sabbath School Convention -- constitution committee meets at Bethel
events.description: The committee appointed to draw up a Constitution and By-Laws for the Sabbath School Convention called to meet at Bethel church on the 8th inst., by order of Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Chairman.

events.name: Confirmation at St. Thomas' Church
events.description: Evening confirmation service at St. Thomas' (Rev. Wm. Alston, rector), attended by the editor. Crowds could not gain admittance. Brother Brown showed the editor to the pulpit; Mrs. Duterte, 'a lady of much distinction', gave him a seat. Alston read the confirmation hymn; Bishop Potter (the Episcopal diocesan) spoke on Melchisedec and addressed the thirty-three candidates, then laid on hands. The editor praises Alston for opposing dancing among his members. Date not stated (Sunday evening before April 4 implied).

events.name: Mass meeting of colored people to fill the 54th Massachusetts, Franklin Hall
events.description: Clipped from a city paper ('held last evening'; date not stated). Hall filled. Officers: President, Rev. Stephen Smith. Vice Presidents: Rev. E. Weaver, Rev. John A. Williams, William E. Gibson [VERIFY], Esq., John Anderson, Esq., D. Colley, David B. Bowser [VERIFY]. Secretaries: Dr. William Ellis, St. George R. Taylor, Dr. Jonathan Davis. Professor Green (colored) said the colored people of Pennsylvania need no longer doubt whether the U.S. will accept black regiments; Gov. Andrew has power to organize one; read extracts from Boston papers and a preamble and resolutions. J. Miller McKim, Esq. said colored enlistments for Pennsylvania had not yet been authorized, urged filling the 54th Massachusetts, noted half the regiment at Readville was recruited in this State. An unnamed colored man spoke on forgiving and rallying to the flag. David Bustill [VERIFY] (colored) said colored people had no rights under the Constitution of Pennsylvania and denounced McKim's sentiments; Professor Green took an opposite view. Robert Purvis spoke, complimenting Secretary Seward. Resolutions read: Massachusetts honored as first in freedom; a full support of the Massachusetts arrangement; a committee to be appointed with power to call another meeting. McKim objected to wording; Green endorsed McKim. Mr. Bustill and Mr. Robert Purvis spoke for adoption (Purvis: not strong enough to enter as a private but hoped to serve). Mr. Stephen Smith took the sense of the meeting and the resolutions were adopted.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church Sabbath School exhibition
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Exhibition of the Union A.M.E. Church Sabbath School on the evening of April 2, 1863, at which an address on 'Youth' was delivered and later printed over the name 'Wm. Tune Simpson' [VERIFY] (dated A. M. E. Union Church, Sabbath School, Phila., Apr. 4th, 1863). The address urges colored youth to study: 'Let no colored boy lay aside his books... He may become a lawyer, a preacher, an educator'.

events.name: Funeral of Rev. Spencer Logan
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia; burial at Lebanon Cemetery (printed 'Libyan Cemetery')
events.description: Rev. Spencer Logan of the Philadelphia Conference died Thursday evening, April 2, 1863 (superannuated after rupturing a blood-vessel nearly two years before); survived by his wife. His remains were taken from his late residence to Bethel Church, Sixth St., where brief remarks were made by Revs. J. P. Campbell and Henry Davis, and conveyed to Lebanon Cemetery (printed 'Libyan Cemetery'), followed by a number of ministers and friends. Funeral date not stated.

events.name: Funeral of Rev. Charles C. Gardiner of Harrisburg
events.location: Rev. Mr. Gibbs' Church (Seventh St. Presbyterian Church), Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Charles C. Gardiner, pastor of the Presbyterian Church (colored), Harrisburg, Pa., died at his residence in Harrisburg on the 6th inst. (April 6, 1863) in his 84th year, of dropsy. His body was brought to Philadelphia and placed in the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church. Described as one of the oldest Presbyterian ministers in the State, a friend to young people and literature, and an early supporter of the Christian Recorder at a Harrisburg meeting three or four years before. He left four or five children. Funeral Thursday, April 9, in Rev. Mr. Gibbs' Church; sermon by Rev. Wm. Catto of New Haven, Conn.; remains deposited in a vault beside the church.

events.name: Zion Wesley Church last quarterly meeting of the year
events.location: Zion Wesley Church, Lombard St., Philadelphia
events.description: Report of the quarterly meeting announced the week before: last Sabbath (April 5, 1863) Rev. Mr. Reeves preached at 10 1/2 a.m., Rev. Mr. Trusty at 3 p.m.; the editor (Weaver) preached the sacramental discourse at night; 'the house was filled'. Pastor Rev. Mr. Williams (John A. Williams).
attendees: pastor (Rev.; printed 'Rev. Mr. Williams' here, full name in the Apr 4 notice)

events.name: Frederick Douglass lecture for the ICY Alumni Association, National Hall
events.description: Frederick Douglass to lecture before the Alumni Association of the Institute for Colored Youth on Friday evening, April 24, 1863, at National Hall, subject 'The Affairs of the Nation'. Admission 25 cents; tickets at the office of the Lebanon Cemetery, 717 Lombard Street, and at Mr. Weaver's Book Store, 619 Pine Street. Doors open 7 1/2, lecture 8 o'clock.

events.name: Camden Circuit fourth quarterly meeting
events.location: Camden Circuit; Quarterly Conference at Macedonia Church; quarterly meeting at Woodbury
events.description: Notice dated April 10th, 1863, signed Peter Gardiner: fourth quarterly meeting of the Camden Circuit commences Friday evening, April 24, continuing nightly to Monday; Quarterly Conference at Macedonia Church Saturday afternoon April 25 at 3 o'clock; quarterly meeting at Woodbury Saturday and Sunday, May 2 and 3.

events.name: Presentation of a suit of clothes to Editor Elisha Weaver by Philadelphia and Germantown women
events.description: On the 1?th of April, 1863 (day blurred), Miss Mary Still, Mrs. Ann Lawe, Mrs. Eliza Stokely, Miss Jane Moulter [VERIFY] of Germantown, and Miss Esther Armstrong of Philadelphia presented Rev. Elisha Weaver, Editor and General Book Steward, a suit of cloth and satin clothes (cost blurred, about $40). Weaver thanks 'Rev. Mrs. Stephen Smith' for encouraging the effort; the committee reported that people of all classes and denominations gave willingly. Jones & Co., 604 Market Street (white clothiers, advertisers), furnished the goods.
attendees: encouraged the gift (printed 'Rev. Mrs. Stephen Smith')

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church Sabbath services (Nazrey, Jones, Catto)
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: On 'last Sabbath' (April 12, 1863): morning, 10 to 12, Rev. James Frisby (local) and Bishop Nazrey officiated; 3 p.m., Rev. Wm. H. Jones of Canada preached; at night Rev. W. Catto (of New Haven, Conn.) preached on 'Keep yourselves in the love of God'. The same Sabbath Weaver administered the Lord's supper at Camden for the indisposed Rev. Peter Gardiner.

events.name: Central Presbyterian Church Sinking Fund Association: Grand Union Levee
events.location: Masonic Hall, South ?th Street, just below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: The Sinking Fund Association of the Lombard Street Central Presbyterian Church gives a grand Union Levee on April 20, 1863, at the Masonic Hall (street number blurred), just below Pine. Tickets $1; single persons 50 cts. The editor regrets he will be absent at Conference.

events.name: West Philadelphia meeting for the 54th Massachusetts (colored volunteers)
events.description: Held 'last Monday evening' (before April 18, 1863; probably April 13). Addresses by Mr. George E. Stephens, Lieutenant Daniel Colley, Prof. A. M. Green and others. Seven of the most promising young men of the place signed as volunteers. Mr. Stephens offered resolutions, passed with barely one dissent; Prof. Green offered a preamble and resolutions (duty of colored men to support the administration; those unable to serve to aid the soldiers; circulars and publication authorized), passed unanimously. Signed Rev. O. M. Robbins [VERIFY], President; M. Gray [VERIFY], Secretary.

events.name: Marriage of William Allen and Anna E. Burton
events.description: April ?th (day blurred), 1863, by Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Mr. William Allen, of Woodbury, N. J., to Miss Anna E. Burton of Philadelphia, Pa.

events.name: Close of A. L. Stanford's pastorate at Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst St.
events.location: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday, April 26, 1863: close of Rev. A. L. Stanford's two-year pastorate. Love feast 10 1/2 a.m. (doors 9 1/2, prayer meeting until the feast); preaching 3 p.m. on 'The three whats connected with the believer's redemption', followed by the Lord's supper; valedictory address 7 1/2 p.m.

events.name: Union and Bethel churches' freedmen relief shipment to Washington
events.location: Philadelphia (to the Union Relief Association, Washington, D.C.)
events.description: Acknowledged by James L. Thomas, Secretary, Union Relief Association, Washington, D.C. (letter dated April 2?th, 1863): from Union Church, Philadelphia (Rev. Henry Davis, pastor), one box and a barrel containing two hundred pieces of men's, women's and children's clothing, hats, bonnets, boots, shoes, bed-quilts, bed-ticks, bolsters, pillow-cases, and five dollars' worth of sugar, tea and rice; from Bethel Church of Philadelphia (Rev. J. P. Campbell, pastor), $12.60 in cash.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church, closing sessions (May 15-19, 1863)
events.description: Continued from the May 16 issue. Friday May 15: Bishop Nazrey in the chair; roll called; the day spent on the Disciplinary questions; some complaints against a few brethren 'amicably settled with a little exception'; some reports. Sunday 10 a.m.: Bishop Nazrey preached the ordination sermon, after which two deacons were ordained (not named). Monday May 18: unfinished business; Conference decided to meet next year in Salem, New Jersey; adjourned to meet the Sabbath schools at 3 o'clock. Tuesday May 19: committee reports, among which the General Book Steward and Editor (Elisha Weaver) made his report, received cordially and adopted; the committee on the crisis reported; at 5 o'clock the Bishop read the appointments (see the appointments event). The same issue (p. 4) prints the Conference's resolutions 'Our Colored Soldiers'. Editorial (p. 2): the Philadelphia Conference brought forward more ten-cent money this year than since 1858 ($47.60 received); the editor says Conference business occupied the paper's last three weeks.
attendees: General Book Steward and editor; made his report

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- 1863 appointments read
events.description: Read by Bishop Nazrey, Tuesday afternoon, 5 o'clock, as printed: Bethel church, J. P. Campbell; Union, A. L. Stanford; Wesley, J. H. Smith; Camden, New Jersey, Henry Davis [VERIFY]; Zion Mission, Wm. D. W. Scharemen [VERIFY]; [illegible]ville Circuit, W. W. Wiader [VERIFY]; Reading, J. R. V. Morgan; Freehold, J. W. Stephenson; Snowhill, Joseph Long; Burlington, Theodore Gould; Bridgeton, Joshua Woodlin; Salem, James Hollen [VERIFY]; Westchester, Jeremiah Young; Frankford, A. C. Crippen; Berks County, Edward Laws [VERIFY]; Danville, John H. Henson [VERIFY]; Lancaster, T. W. Henry; New Brunswick, Wm. Offer [VERIFY]; Bordentown, T. A. Cuff; Oxford, Andrew Till; Cape May, R. Barney [VERIFY]; Woodbury, Jacob Guy [VERIFY]; Trenton, W. Moore; [illegible]ingtonville, J. B. Parker; Princeton, Peter Gardner [VERIFY]; Horntown, John C. Cornish; City Mission, T. H. Cooper. Several names are blurred on the film.

events.name: Sabbath School anniversary before the Philadelphia Annual Conference
events.description: Monday afternoon, 3 o'clock: the church crowded; the Union school led off by singing, represented with two hundred and twenty-five scholars; then Bethel church Sabbath school ('the mammoth school in the city'), Wesley Sabbath school and Zion mission. A Bethel teacher read an essay (printed in the same issue, p. 2 col. 7, signed Drusilla Rodgers [VERIFY]); the Union church followed with another, delivered from memory; the paper hopes to publish 'at least the one delivered by Miss Weere' [VERIFY]. Several brethren addressed the schools; hundreds could not gain admittance. At night the literary society of Bethel church met and was addressed by Rev. J. Brown (printed 'Browe').

events.name: Lecture by William Anderson of Jamaica at Bethel Church
events.location: Announced for Bethel Church, 6th Street; delivered at Wesley Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Mr. William (also printed 'Wilks W.'?) Anderson, of the Island of Jamaica and British Honduras in Central America, at 8 o'clock, on the results of emancipation in those countries and the social and spiritual condition of the colored inhabitants, with a description of the country, climate and productions. Stopping at the Continental Hotel. City ministers asked to announce it from their pulpits. The May 30 issue (p. 2) reports the lecture 'was delivered by the Hon. W. W. Anderson on Monday night at Wesley Church', introduced by the editor (Elisha Weaver); Anderson, a lawyer whose family lives in Jamaica, promoted emigration of laborers to Jamaica; the editor thought the time unfavorable while the country needed every able-bodied colored man. Anderson left for New York on Wednesday.

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School grand concert of vocal music for Wilberforce University
events.description: Given by the teachers and scholars of Bethel Sabbath School in aid of the purchase of Wilberforce University; singing under Prof. H. Shadd; Mr. Seymoor at the piano; doors open half-past 7. Committee: Daniel T. Masten [VERIFY], chairman; Esther Armstrong; Martha Collins; Abram Fields [VERIFY]; James Wiggins [VERIFY]. A separate line on p. 3 says 'The Bethel Exhibition is on Wednesday, the 27th inst., instead of Thursday, the 28th', probably moving this event to May 27. The May 30 issue (p. 2, 'Grand Concert') reports it came off 'on last Wednesday night' (May 27) in Sansom Street Hall: chorus by the scholars conducted by Prof. Hence [sic] Shed of Philadelphia; Mr. Seymour, a young man, at the piano; 'Happy Land' sung by E. Armstrong; Miss Seymour; Miss Maston, a teacher in the Sabbath School; 'our old friends, Mr. Maston, and Wiggins' among the young gentlemen of Bethel Church. Audience smaller than hoped.

events.name: Dr. H. Jerome Brown's lecture on Moral and Intellectual Physiology
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Little Pine street, Philadelphia
events.description: Another of Dr. H. Jerome Brown's scientific lectures, illustrated with life-size paintings; admission free; 8 o'clock. Announced by James Hamilton, pastor.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church: first lecture of a course on affliction
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia
events.description: 10 1/2 a.m.: first lecture of a course on affliction, theme 'The chastening rod in the Father's hand'; 8 p.m.: sermon, 'Angelic Agency'. A. L. Stanford, minister (appointed to Union at the 1863 Conference).

events.name: West Chester circuit quarterly meetings, summer 1863
events.location: West Chester circuit (West Chester, Westtown, Thornbury, Media, Unionville?, Lamberton?)
events.description: West Chester June 13-14; Westtown June 20-21; Thornbury June 27-28; Media July 4-5; 'Uelooville' (Unionville?) July 11-12; Lamberton(?) July 18-19. Jeremiah Young, Elder in Charge; dated West Chester, May 25, 1863.

events.name: Mass meeting of District Grand Lodge No. 2, Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, on the death of Edward M. Thomas
events.location: New Masonic Hall, South 11th st., Philadelphia
events.description: Monday evening. Wm. H. Longfellow chosen chairman; Jonathan Davis secretary; Dr. Jonathan Davis addressed the meeting in tribute to the deceased brother Edward M. Thomas, 'one of the pioneer heroes of our order', who had served six years in the National Grand Council and at his death held its second position. A committee (not named) reported five resolutions: sympathy to the widow and family; a copy with the eulogy to be presented to the widow and relatives at the next grand annual session; a suitable person among the grand officers to prepare a eulogy to be delivered at the next Annual Grand Lodge of the States of Pennsylvania and Delaware. Edward M. Thomas is not linked (residence not stated in the item).

events.name: Supper for the preacher at Jordantown, N.J.
events.description: Supper for the benefit of the preacher realized $28.43, paid to the pastor the same night; the church had raised some $50.00 that year. Committee: Louise Polk [VERIFY], Phillis Cooper, Lucy Amos [VERIFY], Mary A. Green. Letter signed Joseph H. Long, the preacher (appointed to Snowhill at the May 1863 Conference).

events.name: Funeral of Joseph Adams, Haddonfield, N.J.
events.description: Joseph Adams, son of Luke and Phoebe Adams, died April 17, 1863, of consumption; his remains were borne to the grave by the 'United Sons of Truth' Lodge (of which he was a member) and 'Star of Liberty' Lodge, G. U. Order of Odd Fellows, and buried with the honors of the order. Lodge numbers blurred. Memorial verses signed G. B. Miller, Haddonfield, N.J.

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth annual private examination of the senior class
events.description: 'Last week' (early May 1863): written examination in Latin, Greek and Mathematics under Professor Pliny E. Chase, A.M., of Philadelphia; the paper prints the Latin (Virgil, Horace) and mathematics (geometry, plane and spherical trigonometry) questions. The May 30 poem 'To Carrie' names Carrie E. Le Count and James Le Count among the examinees. The May 16 reprint (p. 1) names the five members of the class: Caroline R. Le Count, Rebecca J. Cole, Ellis Yarnell Dingle, James Le Count, Jr., and Joseph Hazzard [VERIFY] Rodgers. (Also named, reading uncertain: Joseph Hazzard Rodgers [VERIFY] (senior-class examinee).)
attendees: senior-class examinee (printed 'James Le Count, Jr.'; the May 30 poem calls him 'junior James Le Count')

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church, first week (May 9-14, 1863)
events.description: The forty-seventh annual conference of the Philadelphia District. Sat. May 9: Bishop Nazrey presiding, assisted by Bishop D. A. Payne; Rev. W. D. W. Schureman elected secretary, Rev. A. L. Stanford assistant; roll called; financial reports; sessions 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.; appointments read 'for quite a number of places, both in and out of the city' (for the Sabbath); benediction by Bishop Payne. Mon. May 11: financial reports finished; the Bishop's address on his travels and on tardy collections, the Wilberforce University; examination of members. Tue. May 12: examination continued; 'some grave complaints' against some brethren ruled out of order by the Bishop. Wed. May 13: further complaints and appointment of committees. Thu. May 14: Bishop Payne brought up the Wilberforce University; the plans approved; the Philadelphia Conference resolved to help buy the property for the connexion; E. Weaver offered a preamble and resolution, amended on motion of Rev. J. P. Campbell to raise the Conference's share to $3,000 instead of $2,000; ministers subscribed from $100 down to $5, between $400 and $500 paid and subscribed; a committee on Education of nine members elected; at 4 p.m. the funeral sermon of the Rev. Richard Robinson (printed 'Rohlosco'/'Robinson') was preached by Henry Davis, assisted by Rev. J. Woodlin. Bishop Quinn expected daily; Bishop Nazrey to devote one night to the Book Concern. Continued in the May 23 issue.

events.name: Funeral sermon of Rev. Richard Robinson at the Philadelphia Conference
events.description: At 4 p.m. during the Conference, the funeral sermon of the Rev. Richard Robinson (died Nov. 18, 1862; the paper's spelling is blurred, 'Robinson'/'Rohinson') was preached by Henry Davis, assisted by Rev. J. Woodlin.

events.name: Lecture by Rev. Mr. Logan at Wesley church
events.description: 'Last Wednesday night' (computed May 13, 1863). The lecturer, a former slave, told of his arrival in Philadelphia: he took a seat in a city street car as he would in New York, Brooklyn, Boston or Pittsburgh, but the conductor asked him to get out and stand on the platform; he asserted his right to ride; the conductor, 'badly frightened', said 'You must go out, I have my bread and butter to make', and he went out after riding nearly to his stop. Printed 'Rev. Mr. Logan' (probably Rev. J. W. Loguen of Syracuse, who attended the A.M.E. Zion conference at Wesley Church the same week; not linked).

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth examination and alumni exercises
events.description: The examination of the pupils came off in the week before May 16; the editor attended the exercises 'on Friday' (May 8 or May 15, 1863, not certain). Opened by the chairman, Mr. Joseph M. White [VERIFY] of the Alumni; Mr. J. C. White, Jr. read an address; Rev. H. H. Garnet of New York delivered the Alumni oration, 'The Scholar, His Field, and His Reward'; an afternoon meeting of the Alumni at 3 o'clock (time blurred); five graduated and received diplomas.

events.name: Prof. P. Houston Murray's lecture on Phrenology
events.description: Tuesday evening; doors open 7, lecture at 8; admission 10 cents. Pastor printed 'Rev. James Underdue' [VERIFY].

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Zion Church (May 2-11, 1863)
events.description: Called to order May 2 by Rev. Joseph J. Clinton, superintendent of the 2d Episcopal District; Rev. J. A. Williams recording secretary, R. A. Gipson(?) assistant. Mon. May 4: Rev. Wm. H. Bishop, senior superintendent, on a fraternal visit; funeral discourses for two deceased members. May 6: Superintendent's money $148.17(?); Lewis Nelson (recommended by the Quarterly Conference of Wesley Church, Philadelphia) and Henry A. Thomas (Timbuctoo Church, N.J.) received on probation; Revs. Schureman, Stanford, and Cornish of the A.M.E. Church introduced and seated; anti-slavery meeting announced. May 7: Rev. J. W. Loguen of the Genesee Conference introduced; anti-slavery meeting (Clinton presiding; Prof. A. M. Green spoke); Sabbath-school anniversary. May 8: business committee's declaration of sentiments on the war, recommending 'patriotic response to the call of the government for able-bodied men... at least, as soldiers' (signed S. T. Jones, chairman, J. D. Brooks, secretary). May 9: Rev. Henry Davis of the Union A.M.E. conference(?) introduced (blurred). May 11: a petition of 105 names praying for the return of John A. Williams to Wesley Church, Philadelphia, and one from Mt. Zion Church for H. H. Blackson(?); S. T. Jones's church-union resolutions adopted. Visitors and members from other places (Harrisburg, Trenton, York, New York) mentioned in text only.
attendees: recording secretary; minister of Wesley Church
received on probation from Wesley Church, Philadelphia

events.name: First Colored Methodist Protestant Church, Pennsylvania District -- Thirteenth Annual Conference
events.description: Opened Saturday May 30, 1863, 5 P.M. Religious services by Rev. Benjamin Scott of the Maryland District; Rev. Abraham Gardiner, President of the District, in the chair. Maryland District clergy seated as corresponding members: Rt. Rev. Nathaniel Peck, President; Revs. Benjamin Scott, James S. Ross, Levi Howard, Solomon Benson, preachers; Bro. Chas. Williams and Bro. Edward Waters Peck (Bro. Edward W. Peck elected Secretary of the Conference). Sabbath appointments: Benezet Hall, 11 A.M., Rev. Nathaniel Peck; 3 P.M., Rev. Benj. Scott; 8 P.M., Rev. Levi Howard; Ebenezer Church, Norristown, 3 P.M., Rev. Solomon Benson; Wesley Chapel, Lombard St., 3 P.M. [VERIFY hour], Bro. Edward W. Peck. Second day (Monday, 10 A.M.): services by Rev. A. Gardiner, prayer by Rev. N. Peck; credentials read of delegates Bro. William Rhodes (Benezet Hall) and Bro. William Simmons (Ebenezer Church, Norristown); resignations of Revs. Thomas Gibbs and James Lober from the connexion received; all members passed the examination of character; sessions open, 10 A.M. to 2 P.M. Appointments: 4 P.M., Rev. J. Ross; 8 P.M., Bro. C. Williams. Reported by Isaiah S. Taylor. Continued (June 20 issue): Third day: Rev. J. S. Taylor introduced Bro. Wm. H. Budd, local preacher from Norristown; Bros. Wm. H. Budd and John H. Harrison examined and received; Revs. Isaiah S. Taylor and J. Addison received as candidates for elders. Fourth day: Rev. Wm. Bowen of the Maryland District received as corresponding member; election of president: Rev. N. Peck judge; candidates A. Gardiner (7), B. Scott (4), W. Bowen (3 [VERIFY]); A. Gardiner re-elected and conducted to the chair by Rev. B. Scott. Fifth day: Budd passed for the itinerancy; Harrison located; thanks to Sister Anna Carpenter and Sister Hannah Gibson. Sixth day: services by Bro. Charles Williams; Rev. J. S. Taylor approved for elder's orders, Rev. John Addison located; Rev. Francis J. Peck of the Maryland District received as corresponding member; Sister Jarena Lee received into the church at the Benezet Hall Station with her local preaching functions. Seventh day, appointments: Norristown Station, Chester and Montgomery County Missions, Rev. Isaiah H. [sic] Taylor; Benezet Hall Station and Philadelphia city Mission, Bro. Wm. H. Budd under the president's supervision; Delaware, Bucks County and New Jersey Missions, Rev. Abraham Gardiner, Rev. John Tangle assistant. Thanks to Sister Eliza Miller and Sister Emma Ringgold. Resolved that the members formerly worshipping in the Israel Church, corner of Fifth and Gaskill Streets, who rejected the Discipline, are expelled (may be received again on acknowledging it). Next conference: last Saturday in May 1864, Norristown. Sabbath appointments: Benezet Hall, 11 A.M. Rev. Solomon Benson, 3 P.M. Rev. William Bowen, 8 P.M. Rev. Benjamin Scott; Ebenezer Church, Norristown, Bro. Charles Williams; Zion Wesley Church, Lombard Street, 3 P.M., Rev. F. J. Peck; John Wesley Church, Shippen Street, Brother Edward W. Peck. Eighth day roll: Elders Rev. Abraham Gardiner (President), Right Rev. Nathaniel Peck, Rev. Benjamin Scott, Rev. William Bowen, Rev. James S. Ross, Rev. Francis J. Peck, Rev. Isaiah S. Taylor; Deacons Rev. Levi Howard, Rev. John Tangle, Rev. John Addison, Rev. Solomon Benson; Preachers Bros. Charles Williams, Edward Waters Peck, William H. Budd, John H. Harrison; Delegates Bros. Wm. Rhodes, Wm. Simmons. Isaiah S. Taylor ordained elder (officiating Revs. N. Peck, B. Scott, A. Gardiner, Wm. Bowen, J. S. Ross). Thanks to Bro. Richard Williams, president of the incorporation of the F.C.M.P. Israel Church, Philadelphia, for defending its rights. Bro. Geo. H. Hutchinson of the A.M.E. Church applied; referred to the Benezet Hall Quarterly Conference. Revs. Thomas Gibbs and James Sober [sic; 'Lober' June 6] declared no longer members. Signed Rev. Abraham Gardiner, President; Rev. Nathaniel Peck, Assistant; Edward W. Peck, Secretary; Isaiah S. Taylor. (The Maryland District clergy are named in text only.)
attendees: Benezet Hall Station and Philadelphia city Mission (Bro.)
president of the incorporation, Israel Church (Bro.)

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church -- Sunday services and lecture on Affiliation
events.description: 10 1/2 A.M. discourse by Rev. Stephen Smith; 8 P.M. second lecture of the course on Affiliation [VERIFY word], theme 'The Stones of the Heavenly temple prepared on earth'.

events.name: Prof. P. Houston Murray's phrenology lecture at the A.M.E. Church, Attleboro
events.description: Monday evening June 1, 1863, lecture on phrenology and philosophy by Prof. P. Houston Murray to a full house; letter signed A. F. Hettrot [VERIFY], Attleboro, Pa.

events.name: Unity Lodge, Grand United Order of Odd Fellows -- anniversary celebration
events.location: National Hall, Market St. above Twelfth, Philadelphia
events.description: Nineteenth [VERIFY] anniversary of Unity Lodge (G.U.O.O.F.) of Pennsylvania, Tuesday night June 9, 1863. Members marched in with regalia about 10:30 P.M., band of musicians, ceremonies; annual oration by the chief, Mr. John C. Bowers. Twelve or fifteen hundred present.

events.name: Dorcas Society of Bethel Church -- Old Folks' Supper
events.description: Thursday June 4, 1863, 5 to 7 P.M. Supper given by the sisters of the Dorcas Society of Bethel for some thirty-five or forty old women aged fifty to eighty, mostly Bethel members, paid out of the sisters' own pockets; one hundred to one hundred and fifty other ladies and gentlemen and ministers of the several denominations attend. No officers named.

events.name: Union A.M.E. and Bethel Sabbath services (City Churches and their Pastors)
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church; Bethel Church; Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday June 7, 1863 (computed from 'last Sabbath'). Union A.M.E.: Brother Stephen Smith preached; Rev. A. L. Stanford, the new pastor, spoke of the Wilberforce collection and the Recorder. Bethel, 3 P.M.: Rev. J. P. Campbell, pastor (reappointed second year); sermon by Rev. Singleton Jones of the Zion Church. Wesley A.M.E., Hurst St., evening: Rev. Joseph Smith, pastor, preached and administered the Lord's Supper.

events.name: Wilberforce Educational Committee, Philadelphia District -- meeting called
events.location: Office of Stephen Smith, 921 Lombard St., Philadelphia

events.name: Colored company enrolled for the defence of the State (Gettysburg emergency)
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: After Gov. Curtin's proclamation calling out the militia against Lee's invasion, the colored citizens of Philadelphia waited on Mayor Henry and the military authorities and were assured colored soldiers would be received and fare the same as other soldiers (blankets and overcoats in the city, arms at Harrisburg). Enrollment began Tuesday June 16, 1863, 7 P.M., at the Philadelphia Institute; Prof. E. D. Bassett took down the names; several addresses urged immediate action. About 10 o'clock Captain Berry, recommended by Mayor Henry (served as captain in the Mexican war and seventeen months in the present war), took command of the colored company; the Mayor requested they start for Harrisburg if a company were raised. By 12 o'clock the company was full and ready to move, but the cars were taken up by white troops, so they had to wait till 10 A.M. (No enlisted men are named. The turning back of the company at Harrisburg is not reported in this issue.)
